sentences.text: Mr. Ayan Bhattacharya  Mr. Anirban Dutta  Mr. Younus Sultan ... for the opposite party no. 2
The petitioner herein has prayed for quashing of  all proceedings of GR Case No. 41 of 2025 presently  pending before learned Additional Chief Judicial  Magistrate, Sealdah.
It is alleged that during the period of 2010 to  2021 a total sum of Rs. 2,59,93,423/- was arranged by  the complainant as investment out of which no principal  amount was reverted to gain faith.
It is further alleged that complainant rendered  rent payment for one office space utilized by the petitioner  at 42/A, Putin Khatik Road, but the same was not paid.

It  was claimed that for such act on the part of the petitioner,
 the complainant suffered decline in goodwill.
It is also alleged that the work orders and the  client names were forged.

sentences.text: The complainant suppressed the material facts and has initiated the instant proceeding.
The investigating agency did not make any preliminary enquiry before starting investigation.

Therefore, he submits that continuance of further proceedings under sections 120B/420/406/467/468/471/506 of the Indian Penal Code against the petitioner will be a mere abuse of the process of the court.
Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner, the application is admitted.

Petitioner is directed to serve a copy of application upon the State through the office of the Public Prosecutor, High Court, Calcutta and upon the learned counsel appeared for the opposite party no.
2, in course of the day.
Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 seeks to file affidavit-in-opposition.
Let such affidavit-in-opposition be filed within four weeks from date.

Reply, if any, to be filed within two weeks thereafter.
Let the matter be listed under the heading "Contested Application" on 21st May, 2026.

(Dr. Ajoy Kumar Mukherjee, J.)
